terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase, the front part of the arm, after classical prīmōris, foremost (dentēs prīmōrēs, the front teeth, Plin. NH 7.70; Lewis & Short). Classical Latin has no plain word for the wrist: the Romans spoke of the hand, manus, or of bracchium.
The anatomists’ word, from Greek καρπός; not in Lewis & Short in this sense (there Carpus is a carver in Petronius).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 59, 409, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).

phrases.latin: manicae prōlixae ūsque in prīmōrēs manūs
phrases.english: sleeves reaching all the way to the wrists
